cases.heading: False or Misleading Risk Presentation
cases.claim: TV ad omits the contraindication for known hypersensitivity to glucagon or excipients and the W&P for hypersensitivity and allergic reactions; includes pheochromocytoma and insulinoma contraindications without the consequences (dramatic BP increase; hypoglycemia).
cases.rationale: Omitting serious risks and material facts suggests Gvoke is safer than demonstrated.
cases.check: Rule: every contraindication and W&P in the PI must appear; contraindications should state consequences where the PI does.

cases.cat: Overstatement of efficacy (ease of use / administration)
cases.heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
cases.claim: “Easy to use. Easy to know you did it right. Pretty easy, huh?”
cases.context: PI/IFU describe multiple preparation and administration steps; no signal to confirm correct administration; no supporting references.
cases.rationale: Ease-of-use and 'did it right' claims unsupported and oversimplify emergency administration.
cases.check: Do ease-of-use claims oversimplify administration relative to the IFU, or claim user confirmation the device does not provide?

cases.cat: Minimization of disease seriousness / omission of material facts
cases.heading: Omission of Material Fact
cases.claim: VOICEOVER (VO): “If you have diabetes and take insulin, you know low blood sugar can be scary. You might start to sweat, panic, worry you might pass out. You may even feel like you’re falling.” | “I can be used even before passing out.”
cases.context: Indication is severe hypoglycemia (confusion, seizures, unconsciousness, death); IFU says not for cases where sugar can be taken by mouth; severe hypoglycemia requires help of others.
cases.rationale: Presents mild symptoms only and omits when to administer and need for administration by others.
cases.check: Does the piece depict the condition in a milder form than the indicated population, or omit who must administer and when?
